links.outcome: Answer performance of ontology-grounded agentic RAG versus other RAG methods on ontology and medical QA benchmarks
links.effect: OA-RAG achieved the best overall performance among evaluated ontology-fine-tuned and popular RAG methods, especially on reasoning-intensive tasks. It was competitive with, and sometimes better than, textbook-based domain RAG systems.
links.quote: Across benchmarks derived from three large-scale ontologies and six real-world medical question-answering tasks, OA-RAG achieves the best overall performance among the evaluated ontology-fine-tuned and popular RAG methods, with particularly strong results on reasoning-intensive tasks.

links.outcome: Whether model-assessed grounding levels indicate answer reliability (association with accuracy)
links.effect: Stronger reported grounding levels (entailed, supported, related, unrelated) were generally associated with higher accuracy. No numeric values are given in the abstract.
links.quote: The reported grounding levels also offer a useful indication of answer reliability, with stronger grounding generally associated with higher accuracy.

unlisted_practices: Ontology-based formal reasoning combined with LLM reasoning as a grounding knowledge source

screen.reason: The paper develops and benchmarks a new agentic ontology-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework (OA-RAG) on medical QA benchmarks; it does not evaluate an organizational deployment practice or safeguard added to an existing deployed tool.
